name: infrastructure
description: Roads, rails, bridges, poles and other public works.
conventions: Linear objects (roads, rails, fences) are built as a repeatable segment with matching ends, so segments tile along z.
anticipate: A segment that tiles end to end, plus curved or junction variants.
Collision and navigation surfaces separate from the visual mesh.

name: road

scale.source: lane width about 2.75-3.75 m (general knowledge: design guides differ per country); a segment is as long as you choose

pitfalls: Segments must have identical cross-sections at both ends, or seams show.
Lane markings are a decal or texture, not geometry, or they z-fight with the surface.

parts.name: Leaf
parts.note: A bascule bridge leaf hinges about a horizontal axis at its end.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard

name: railway track

scale.source: ballast bed width, general knowledge; gauge is 1.435 m (UIC standard)

anticipate: Standard gauge is 1.435 m between the inner rail edges (UIC/IEC standard); sleepers about 0.6 m apart (general knowledge); the ballast bed is about 3.4-4.5 m wide.

name: street lamp
description: A lamp post or street light.

parts.name: Lamp
parts.note: Emissive material plus a light node at the bulb.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard

name: fence

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard

anticipate: A repeatable bay with a post at each end.

parts.name: Post
parts.note: Posts at the ends and between sections; set into the ground.

name: crash barrier
description: A motorsport barrier beside a race track: stacked steel W-beams (Armco) on posts, often with a catch fence behind it. A guard rail along a public road is infrastructure.guard-rail.

parts.name: Post
parts.note: Steel posts about every 2 m (guardrail) or 4 m (catch fence).

parts.name: Rail
parts.note: The W-beam is about 0.31 m high with its centre about 0.55-0.75 m above the ground; motorsport uses two or three stacked.

scale.source: general knowledge: road and motorsport guardrail sections; not a standard

anticipate: A repeatable section with a post at each end; tile sections along the edge of the run-off area, not along the track edge.

name: race kerb
description: A low red-and-white kerb at the edge of a race track in a corner.

parts.name: Block
parts.note: Alternating red and white blocks about 1-1.5 m long; the kerb rises a few centimetres towards the outside.

scale.source: general knowledge: circuit kerbs; not a standard

anticipate: Kerbs run on the inside of a corner along the apex and on the outside at the exit; they lie on the track surface, not on the grass.

name: power pylon
description: A high-voltage pylon or utility pole.

scale.source: general knowledge: typical production range, not a standard: wooden poles 8-15 m, lattice pylons 25-70 m

parts.name: Leg
parts.note: The lattice legs lean in towards the top.

name: traffic sign
description: A road sign on a pole: a round, triangular or square plate with a reflective face.

parts.name: Pole
parts.note: A round steel tube, about 76 mm across in many European countries.

parts.name: Plate
parts.note: Front face reflective and facing the traffic; the back is plain metal with the mounting clamps.

scale.source: general knowledge: round signs of about 0.6, 0.7 or 0.9 m; the lower edge of the plate about 2.2 m above a footpath in built-up areas and lower (about 1.5-1.8 m) along rural roads; rules differ per country

conventions: The plate faces the traffic it is meant for, on the right of the carriageway in right-hand traffic, set back a little from the edge of the road.
pitfalls: Text and symbols on many signs: use a texture, a decal or a distance-field shader, not one mesh per letter.
Hundreds of identical signs: one MultiMesh per kind of plate, not hundreds of MeshInstance3D nodes.

name: guard rail
description: A steel road safety barrier: a corrugated beam on posts along the edge of a road. A motorsport barrier with a catch fence is infrastructure.crash-barrier.

scale.source: general knowledge: the beam about 0.3 m deep with its top near 0.75 m, posts every 2 to 4 m; national standards differ

conventions: Built as a repeatable segment along z whose length is a whole number of post spacings, so segments tile.
The ends are sloped or curved away from the traffic, never a blunt beam end facing it.
pitfalls: A blunt end facing the traffic is the classic mistake; taper it down to the ground over several metres.
Collision: overlap the boxes of neighbouring segments a little, or a fast car slips through the seam.

name: delineator post
description: A small white roadside post with a reflector that marks the edge of the road at night.

parts.name: Reflector
parts.note: Retroreflective; in a game an emissive or very bright material that only shows in headlight range.

scale.source: general knowledge: about 1 m above the verge, every 50 m or so on rural roads; rules differ per country

pitfalls: Thousands of them along a road network: one MultiMesh per road tile, with a short visibility range.
